newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan recommends U.N. observer mission for Angola.
newsitem.headline: Annan recommends U.N. observer mission for Angola.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Monday that the Security Council renew the mandate of the U.N. peacekeeping force in Angola until June 30 and that it be transformed into a U.N. observer mission beginning July 1.

The force, called the U.N. Angola Verification Mission (UNAVEM III), has been helping implement a 1994 peace accord ending nearly two decades of civil war between the formerly Marxist Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA), headed by President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, and former rebels of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA), led by Jonas Savimbi.
A high point of the peace process was the swearing-in last Friday of a government of unity and national reconciliation that includes representatives of both parties.
Annan did not say how large the proposed U.N. Observer Mission in Angola (UNOMA) should be.

UNAVEM III, which had a maximum strength of more than 7,000 and is now down to about 5,500, was last renewed for only a couple of weeks, until April 16, while the Security Council kept a close watch on whether the unity government would finally be established after repeated delays.

Annan said the observer mission should help oversee remaining military provisions of the peace agreement and focus on political, police, human rights, humanitarian and public informations issues to help consolidate the process of reconciliation.
In an upbeat report to the Security Council, he said developments over the last two weeks had been "very encouraging."
"Never before has the country been so close to the final resolution of its devastating conflict and to the attainment of lasting peace," he wrote.
"The Angolan people and their leaders should be congratulated on their determination, patience and perseverance."
Annan said he hoped rapid progress could now be made in completing other aspects of the peace accord in a spirit of cooperation and mutual accommodation.

He also hoped that a long-awaited meeting between President dos Santos and Savimbi would soon take place, "in order to consolidate the progress which has been achieved towards national reconciliation."
